front.title: An Intent Translator for Hallucination Mitigation in an Agentic AI Framework

author.organization: Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust

abstract.t: This document proposes an Intent Translator to mitigate hallucination in the intent translation in an Agentic AI Framework. This Intent Translator has an agentic AI workflow for detecting and mitigating structural and semantic errors, including hallucinated policy content, when translating a natural-language network intent into a structured policy. The workflow coordinates role-specialized language-model functions with deterministic validation tools within a predefined action space and a bounded retry budget. Schema- constrained generation limits structural defects, while cross-slot checks and intent-faithfulness assessment identify a potentially unsupported or inconsistent policy content. Structured validation traces guide targeted re-extraction and regeneration. Unresolved cases retain explicit failure status for downstream review. This document describes component interactions in the Intent Translator, validation outcomes, and recovery behavior. It also presents a 3GPP TS 28.312-based instantiation for mobile network management.
